Definition: of Hebrew origin (H4519); Mannasses (i.e. Menashsheh), an Israelite:--Manasses.
BiblicalUsage: Manassēs is Manasseh, the king in Matthew's genealogy and the tribe sealed in Revelation. In Matthew 1:10 Ezekias begets Manasses, and Manasses begets Amon, and in Revelation 7:6 twelve thousand of the tribe of Manasses are sealed. The name runs from a wicked king to a sealed tribe.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Manassēs shows me that God keeps a place for a tribe whose king did great evil, and I hold that His sealing grace reaches further than any family history.
